newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TO RACE 200 METRES IN BRUSSELS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JOHNSON TO RACE 200 METRES IN BRUSSELS.

text.p: Michael Johnson, his place as world number one over 400 metres secure after retaining his world title on Tuesday, now seeks top billing over the 200.
The double Olympic champion has been ranked first in the world over 400 for the past four years and top of the 200 ranking for three consecutive years.
"I would like to continue to be ranked number one in the 400 and 200," Johnson said on Wednesday. "If I don't, that's okay."

His manager Brad Hunt said the double Olympic champion would race over 400 metres in the Zurich meeting on August 13, then turn to the 200 at the U.S.-British duel in London on August 17 and at meetings in Malmo and Brussels. Berlin was also likely to be on the American's schedule.
"There probably will be at least one more 400 this year," said Johnson, who seems eager to race after three weeks of hard training prior to the world championships.

The world title, Johnson's fifth in individual events, marked a major turnaround in a season which went awry for the 29-year-old when he was injured in his June 1 showdown over 150 metres with Canadian Donovan Bailey.
He then lost a 400 metres race for the first time in eight years in Paris on June 25.
Johnson, who gained a late entry into the world championships as a defending champion, declined to call the win more special than his double gold at Atlanta.
But it was certainly was more scary. A leg cramp in the final turn caused Johnson some anxious moments before he was able to shake it off and power to victory.
Johnson said his left leg was still sore and and treatment would continue this week.
"We'll wait until Friday to see how it goes," he said about the possibility of running on the U.S. 4x400-metre relay at the weekend.
Meantime, his distinctive deep voice and knowledge of the sport will be put to work as Johnson comments on and analyses races for the NBC television network.
"Nerve-racking," Johnson said of his new venture.
There are no plans, however, to head off to Hollywood to make movies. Neither does Johnson expect to experiment with other events on the track.
"I won't be moving to any other event outside the 200 or 400 from now until the end of my career," said Johnson, who in the past has dabbled with the 100 metres in non-championship years.
He obviously would like to smash compatriot Butch Reynolds's 400 metres world record, but makes no predictions.
"Any time I go out, I give 100 per cent effort," Johnson said. "If I go out and say I'm going to make an assault on the world record, then what was I doing in the previous races?"
